soru: What are the most important works and open problems in non-invasive EEG brain-computer interfaces with deep learning?

alt_sorular.soru: What are the foundational paradigms and classic (pre-deep-learning) signal processing and classification methods for non-invasive EEG BCIs?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers the seminal BCI definition and review papers, the main paradigms (MI, P300/ERP, SSVEP) and the classic CSP/FBCSP, xDAWN, CCA and Riemannian baselines that deep models are compared against.

alt_sorular.soru: What are the main deep learning architecture families for EEG decoding (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, GNNs, hybrid models)?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers the canonical CNN models (EEGNet, Shallow/Deep ConvNet), key Transformer and hybrid models (e.g. EEG Conformer), and representative graph and recurrent approaches, along with systematic reviews of deep learning for EEG.

alt_sorular.soru: How are self-supervised learning, pretraining and large EEG foundation models used for brain-computer interfaces?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers the major self-supervised and pretrained EEG models (BENDR, BIOT, LaBraM, EEGPT, CBraMod and similar) and benchmarks that evaluate how well they generalize.

alt_sorular.soru: How do deep EEG-BCI methods handle cross-subject and cross-session variability (transfer learning, domain adaptation, calibration reduction)?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers the main transfer learning and domain adaptation reviews and methods, including alignment-based approaches and subject-independent deep models, along with evidence on how much calibration they save.

alt_sorular.soru: Which datasets, benchmarks, software libraries and evaluation protocols are standard, and what reproducibility issues exist?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers the standard public datasets (BCI IV 2a/2b, PhysioNet MI, OpenBMI, TUH, SEED, DEAP), benchmarking frameworks such as MOABB and braindecode, and critiques of evaluation practice such as data leakage and within-subject versus cross-subject splits.

alt_sorular.soru: What are the key applications of deep EEG BCIs (motor imagery control, speech/imagined speech decoding, visual/semantic decoding, emotion, rehabilitation)?
sorgular: imagined speech EEG decoding deep learning
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers representative high-impact application papers for motor control and rehabilitation, speech and language decoding, visual and image decoding, and affective BCIs, including critiques of the claims made in EEG-to-text work.

alt_sorular.soru: What are the open problems: robustness, interpretability, BCI illiteracy, adversarial vulnerability, real-time online use, and privacy and ethics?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers surveys and key studies on open challenges, including non-stationarity, BCI inefficiency, adversarial attacks, explainability, online evaluation, and privacy or ethical concerns, plus forward-looking roadmap papers.

alt_sorular.soru: Which adjacent-area methods (sleep staging, clinical EEG and seizure detection, MEG and fMRI decoding, time-series foundation models) are reused in EEG-BCI deep learning?
sorgular: MEG decoding speech perception deep learning
alt_sorular.yeterli: Covers the adjacent works whose architectures, pretraining schemes, or data augmentation methods are directly borrowed by EEG-BCI deep learning, such as MEG speech decoding, sleep staging nets and EEG augmentation studies.

calismalar.baslik: EEGNet: a compact convolutional neural network for EEG-based brain–computer interfaces
calismalar.gerekce: Introduces EEGNet, the canonical compact CNN designed to classify EEG signals accurately across different BCI paradigms.
calismalar.alinti: Here, we ask if we can design a single CNN architecture to accurately classify EEG signals from different BCI paradigms

calismalar.baslik: Deep learning with convolutional neural networks for EEG decoding and visualization
calismalar.gerekce: Foundational deep ConvNet decoding paper showing batch normalization, ELUs and cropped training boosted performance, benchmarked against FBCSP.
calismalar.alinti: Our results show that recent advances from the machine learning field, including batch normalization and exponential linear units, together with a cropped training strategy, boosted the deep ConvNets decoding performance

calismalar.baslik: Brain–computer interfaces for communication and control
calismalar.gerekce: Foundational review of brain-computer interfaces for communication and control, anchoring the field's core paradigms.

calismalar.baslik: A review of classification algorithms for EEG-based brain–computer interfaces: a 10 year update
calismalar.gerekce: Surveys BCI and machine learning literature from 2007 to 2017, covering classic and newer EEG classification approaches.
calismalar.alinti: We surveyed the BCI and machine learning literature from 2007 to 2017 to identify the new classification approaches that have been investigated to design BCIs.

calismalar.baslik: Deep learning-based electroencephalography analysis: a systematic review
calismalar.gerekce: Systematic review of 156 papers applying deep learning to EEG between 2010 and 2018, including BCI applications.
calismalar.alinti: we review 156 papers that apply DL to EEG, published between January 2010 and July 2018

calismalar.baslik: Filter Bank Common Spatial Pattern (FBCSP) in Brain-Computer Interface
calismalar.gerekce: Introduces Filter Bank Common Spatial Pattern, a foundational classic spatial-filtering method for BCIs.

calismalar.baslik: Multiclass Brain–Computer Interface Classification by Riemannian Geometry
calismalar.gerekce: Establishes Riemannian geometry for multiclass BCI classification, a major classic method family.

calismalar.baslik: MOABB: Trustworthy algorithm benchmarking for BCIs
calismalar.gerekce: MOABB benchmarking framework analyzing decoding algorithms across 12 open datasets with over 250 subjects; core reproducibility resource.
calismalar.alinti: To validate our efforts, we analyze a set of state-of-the-art decoding algorithms across 12 open access datasets, with over 250 subjects

calismalar.baslik: BENDR: using transformers and a contrastive self-supervised learning task to learn from massive amounts of EEG data
calismalar.gerekce: BENDR adapts speech-recognition style transformers and contrastive self-supervised learning to learn from massive amounts of EEG data.
calismalar.alinti: We specifically adapt an approach effectively used for automatic speech recognition, which similarly (to LMs) uses a self-supervised training objective to learn compressed representations of raw data signals

calismalar.baslik: Large Brain Model for Learning Generic Representations with Tremendous EEG Data in BCI
calismalar.gerekce: Large Brain Model aims for universal EEG perceptual capabilities through unsupervised pre-training on tremendous EEG data.
calismalar.alinti: We hope that LEMs can break through the limitations of different task types of EEG datasets, and obtain universal perceptual capabilities of EEG signals through unsupervised pre-training.

calismalar.baslik: CBraMod: A Criss-Cross Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
calismalar.gerekce: CBraMod proposes a criss-cross brain foundation model for EEG decoding amid growing EEG foundation-model research.
calismalar.alinti: With the success of large language models, there is a growing body of studies focusing on EEG foundation models.

calismalar.baslik: EEG Conformer: Convolutional Transformer for EEG Decoding and Visualization
calismalar.gerekce: EEG Conformer is a convolutional transformer hybrid for EEG decoding and visualization, a highly cited architecture.

calismalar.baslik: Transfer Learning for Brain-Computer Interfaces: A Euclidean Space Data Alignment Approach
calismalar.gerekce: Proposes Euclidean-space alignment of EEG trials across subjects to improve learning for a new subject; widely used transfer preprocessing.
calismalar.alinti: We propose a novel approach to align EEG trials from different subjects in the Euclidean space to make them more similar, and hence improve the learning performance for a new subject

calismalar.baslik: Transfer Learning for EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interfaces: A Review of Progress Made Since 2016
calismalar.gerekce: Reviews transfer learning for EEG BCIs since 2016, using data from other subjects, sessions or devices to reduce calibration.
calismalar.alinti: Transfer learning (TL), which utilizes data or knowledge from similar or relevant subjects/sessions/devices/tasks to facilitate learning for a new subject/session/device/task, is frequently used to reduce the amount of calibration effort

calismalar.baslik: Uncovering the structure of clinical EEG signals with self-supervised learning
calismalar.gerekce: Investigates self-supervised learning to discover structure in unlabeled clinical EEG, bridging adjacent clinical domain and representation learning.
calismalar.alinti: We investigated self-supervised learning (SSL), a promising technique for discovering structure in unlabeled data, to learn representations of EEG signals

calismalar.baslik: Neuro-GPT: Towards A Foundation Model for EEG
calismalar.gerekce: Neuro-GPT foundation model pre-trained on large-scale data via self-supervised reconstruction of masked EEG segments.
calismalar.alinti: The foundation model is pre-trained on a large-scale data set using a self-supervised task that learns how to reconstruct masked EEG segments

calismalar.baslik: EEGPT: Pretrained Transformer for Universal and Reliable Representation of EEG Signals
calismalar.gerekce: EEGPT presents a pretrained transformer for universal and reliable representations of EEG signals.

calismalar.baslik: BIOT: Biosignal Transformer for Cross-data Learning in the Wild
calismalar.gerekce: BIOT biosignal transformer enables cross-data learning from heterogeneous EEG recordings in the wild.

calismalar.baslik: EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
calismalar.gerekce: Provides a three-paradigm EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox while investigating general, severe cases of BCI illiteracy.
calismalar.alinti: we looked for more general, severe cases of BCI illiteracy than have been previously reported in the literature

calismalar.baslik: EEG datasets for motor imagery brain–computer interface
calismalar.gerekce: Widely used 52-subject motor imagery EEG dataset accompanied by psychological and physiological questionnaire results.
calismalar.alinti: Here we present not only EEG datasets for MI BCI from 52 subjects, but also the results of a psychological and physiological questionnaire

calismalar.baslik: The Temple University Hospital EEG Data Corpus
calismalar.gerekce: Temple University Hospital EEG corpus, a large clinical EEG resource used for pretraining foundation models.

calismalar.baslik: Cross-Dataset Variability Problem in EEG Decoding With Deep Learning
calismalar.gerekce: Addresses the cross-dataset variability problem in EEG decoding with deep learning, a key generalization issue.

calismalar.baslik: Decoding speech perception from non-invasive brain recordings
calismalar.gerekce: Decodes perceived speech from non-invasive recordings of a large cohort using contrastive learning on self-supervised representations.
calismalar.alinti: Here, we introduce a model trained with contrastive-learning to decode self-supervised representations of perceived speech from the non-invasive recordings of a large cohort of healthy individuals.

calismalar.baslik: Visual Decoding and Reconstruction via EEG Embeddings with Guided Diffusion
calismalar.gerekce: EEG-based visual decoding and reconstruction using EEG embeddings with guided diffusion, motivated by fMRI's cost and temporal limitations.
calismalar.alinti: However, the high cost and low temporal resolution of fMRI limit their applications in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), prompting a high need for visual decoding based on electroencephalography (EEG).

calismalar.baslik: Evaluating Robustness and Detection of Adversarial Attacks in EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interfaces
calismalar.gerekce: Evaluates adversarial attacks on EEG-BCI classifiers, which can compromise accuracy, safety and user privacy.
calismalar.alinti: Machine learning classifiers used in BCIs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, which can compromise accuracy, safety, and user privacy.

calismalar.baslik: On using AI for EEG-based BCI applications: problems, current challenges and future trends
calismalar.gerekce: Discusses problems, current challenges and future trends of AI-based EEG BCIs, including hurdles for foundational models' reliability.
calismalar.alinti: Applying AI to real-world EEG-based BCIs, particularly in building powerful foundational models, presents unique and intricate hurdles that could affect their reliability

calismalar.baslik: A large-scale evaluation framework for EEG deep learning architectures
calismalar.gerekce: Large-scale evaluation framework for EEG deep learning architectures across six classification problems, supporting reproducible benchmarking.
calismalar.alinti: This framework comprises (i) a collection of EEG datasets currently including 100 examples (recording sessions) from six different classification problems

calismalar.baslik: Calibration-free online test-time adaptation for electroencephalography motor imagery decoding
calismalar.gerekce: Calibration-free online test-time adaptation for motor imagery decoding that preserves privacy by not accessing source data.
calismalar.alinti: Our approach guarantees the preservation of privacy by eliminating the requirement to access the source data during the adaptation process.

calismalar.baslik: What does my network learn? Assessing interpretability of deep learning for EEG
calismalar.gerekce: Assesses interpretability of deep learning for EEG by examining what ResNet and EEGNet models learn.
calismalar.alinti: We trained two convolutional neural networks (CNN): (1) ResNet, a residual network, and (2) EEGNet, which leverages spatiotemporal properties of EEG.

calismalar.baslik: A large EEG dataset for studying cross-session variability in motor imagery brain-computer interface
calismalar.gerekce: Large multi-day motor imagery dataset for studying cross-session variability, a long-standing BCI challenge.
calismalar.alinti: the classification of motor imagery (MI) from electroencephalography (EEG) across multiple days is a long-standing challenge due to the large variability of the EEG signals.
